description: Local-only LLM router. Zero network egress beyond explicitly-configured upstream baseUrl. No telemetry, no wallet, no payment processing.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Read scoring + tiers + providers config. Hot-reloaded every 2s.
expectedBehaviors.justification: The router is config-driven; without reading config there is no scoring or routing.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Installer reads scripts/install.sh to copy server.js + config.json into ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/router/.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Install path is set by the operator; the script reads its own source location via $0.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Install script writes the systemd unit so the router starts on boot.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Standard OpenClaw plugin installation pattern. The script requires sudo at install time per operator consent.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Installer writes the operator-chosen env values (API keys, host overrides) to a 0600 file the systemd unit reads via EnvironmentFile=.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Avoids embedding env values in the unit file body (and the bash subshell that writes it). The file is chmod 0600.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Install script edits the OpenClaw gateway config to register 'openclaw-router' as a model provider with api='openai-chat-completions'.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Required for OpenClaw to discover the router. Idempotent — only adds if missing.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Read at runtime to attach Authorization: Bearer header to upstream OpenAI requests.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Operator-supplied key. Never written to disk in plaintext by the router (read from env at request time).

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Bearer key for OpenRouter upstream tier.
expectedBehaviors.justification: Same as above. Only read if the provider's apiKeyEnv matches.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Bearer key for z.ai GLM upstream tier.
Bearer key for Moonshot Kimi upstream tier.
Proxy each AI request to the upstream selected by the scorer.
expectedBehaviors.justification: The router's only purpose. baseUrl is operator-controlled via config.json. Default config has only public LLM endpoints + 127.0.0.1. An upstreamAllowlist field is documented (config.json) but not enforced; design choice pending operator policy.

expectedBehaviors.purpose: Started by systemd as the openclaw-router.service unit; binds 127.0.0.1:8402 only.

securityNotes: The router is bound to 127.0.0.1 only — not reachable from external hosts.
API keys are read from env at request time, never written to disk by the router process.
config.json is the operator's contract. The router hot-reloads it but the file's permissions are entirely the operator's responsibility.

The router does NOT enforce an upstream URL allowlist today. The config schema documents an `upstreamAllowlist` field as a TODO. Operators running on shared hosts should deploy with an outbound proxy or OS-level network policy (e.g. nftables) to constrain the router's egress.
Request bodies are capped at 10 MiB (ROUTER_MAX_BODY env to override). Upstream sockets are capped at 120s/request. Listener at 5min/connection.
systemd's EnvironmentFile= is used (not inline Environment= directives) so env values are not exposed to the bash process that writes the unit file.
No telemetry, no analytics, no external telemetry endpoints. The router does not phone home.
No subprocess invocations from the server runtime. The install.sh script is operator-run only.
references: https://github.com/BlockRunAI/ClawRouter (inspiration for the plugin schema; we do not use it)
